sub: Most studies looked at joint pain and stiffness

reviewVerdict.text: A 2026 review that combined 10 earlier reviews on curcumin for knee osteoarthritis found meaningful improvement in pain and stiffness, similar to common anti-inflammatory drugs, with fewer side effects reported.
reviewVerdict.caveat: only 3 of the 10 reviews were rated high quality
reviewVerdict.source: Frontiers in Pharmacology, umbrella review, Jan 2026

sub: Studied mostly as an absorption enhancer added to other supplements, not as a supplement on its own
Strong evidence for correcting low levels; mixed evidence for other uses
studiedAmount: 600-4,000 IU per day, depending on your starting level

reviewVerdict.text: A Cochrane review of vitamin D supplementation trials found it does not clearly reduce the risk of fractures or falls in generally healthy older adults who aren't already deficient — the clearest benefit shows up in people who start out with low levels.
reviewVerdict.caveat: trials used different doses and forms of vitamin D, and results were more positive for people with confirmed deficiency
reviewVerdict.source: Cochrane Database of Systematic Reviews, vitamin D for prevention of fractures and falls

sub: Best evidence is for people with a real magnesium shortage
Best evidence is for lowering triglycerides (a type of fat in the blood)

reviewVerdict.text: A 2020 Cochrane review pooling dozens of trials found that omega-3 supplements probably have little or no effect on the risk of heart attack, stroke, or cardiovascular death overall, though they do reliably lower triglyceride levels.
reviewVerdict.caveat: the benefit was more solid for triglycerides than for actual heart attack or stroke outcomes
reviewVerdict.source: Cochrane Database of Systematic Reviews, omega-3 fatty acids for cardiovascular disease prevention

sub: Best evidence is for jet lag and shifting sleep timing
studiedAmount: 0.5-5 mg — timing matters more than the amount

reviewVerdict.text: A Cochrane review of melatonin for jet lag concluded it's remarkably effective at reducing jet lag symptoms and speeding recovery when timed correctly around the destination's night-time, and that it appears safe for occasional short-term use.
reviewVerdict.caveat: timing mattered more than dose, and results were less consistent for east-to-west travel
reviewVerdict.source: Cochrane Database of Systematic Reviews, melatonin for jet lag

sub: Best evidence is for preventing diarrhea from antibiotic use
studiedAmount: 1-10 billion CFU per day in most trials; this product is higher

reviewVerdict.text: A Cochrane review of probiotics for preventing antibiotic-associated diarrhea found a moderate protective effect, mainly in trials using Lactobacillus- or Saccharomyces-containing strains.
reviewVerdict.caveat: benefits varied a lot by which strains were used, so results don't automatically apply to every probiotic product
reviewVerdict.source: Cochrane Database of Systematic Reviews, probiotics for antibiotic-associated diarrhea

Best evidence is for shortening the common cold when started early
studiedAmount: 75 mg or more per day, started within 24 hours of symptoms

reviewVerdict.text: A systematic review of zinc for the common cold found that lozenges or syrup started within a day of symptoms starting may shorten how long a cold lasts by roughly a day, though results varied a lot between individual trials.
reviewVerdict.caveat: most trials used zinc lozenges or syrup rather than capsules like this one, so how well the finding carries over to this form isn't fully clear
reviewVerdict.source: Systematic review, zinc for the common cold

sub: Doesn't prevent colds for most people, but may modestly shorten how long one lasts

reviewVerdict.text: A Cochrane review of vitamin C trials found that regularly taking it doesn't reduce how often the average person catches a cold, but it modestly shortens how long a cold lasts once you have one.
reviewVerdict.caveat: a reduced-incidence effect was only seen in people under major physical stress, like marathon runners or soldiers in cold climates
reviewVerdict.source: Cochrane Database of Systematic Reviews, vitamin C for preventing and treating the common cold
